builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs
summary: HiSA replaces the full query-key dot product in RoPE attention with a static, parameter-free partial dot product over the hidden dimension, rather than sparsifying over tokens. The cost is that the model must be trained with HiSA from scratch (or with the provided FlashAttention-3 kernels); it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and it adds a custom kernel dependency. What can fail after adoption is portability and compatibility: gains depend on the custom FA3 kernel path, downstream fine-tunes of dense models cannot use it, and quality results are demonstrated on the authors' own training runs rather than established benchmarks at production scale.
rationale: HiSA requires training from scratch with custom kernels, so the reader can only apply it when pretraining or heavily retraining their own small models, and otherwise must wait for pretrained HiSA checkpoints or API support.

claims.statement: HiSA replaces the full query-key dot product in RoPE attention with a static, parameter-free partial dot product over the hidden dimension, rather than sparsifying over tokens. The cost is that the model must be trained with HiSA from scratch (or with the provided FlashAttention-3 kernels); it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and it adds a custom kernel dependency. What can fail after adoption is portability and compatibility: gains depend on the custom FA3 kernel path, downstream fine-tunes of dense models cannot use it, and quality results are demonstrated on the authors' own training runs rather than established benchmarks at production scale.

Trained from scratch, HiSA matches or exceeds dense-attention quality while computing only about one third of the query-key products, with reported decoding speedups and smaller memory footprint at inference.
